data.body:
CORRECTION to the '## Prior art considered' section added to this description. It was written in response to a T1 plan-review finding AFTER the mechanism was designed and landed - not at design time. Its phrasing ('were weighed rather than ignored') overstates what happened. Truthful account: the four fields were derived directly from the three escapes this epic documents; I did not consult in-toto, SLSA or W3C PROV while designing them. The comparison is post-hoc, and presenting it as design-time deliberation is exactly the 'confidence outrunning method' failure this epic exists to close - it should not stand unqualified in this epic of all epics.

The SUBSTANCE holds and is worth keeping: build-provenance predicates answer 'did this artifact come from that source', not 'could this measurement have failed for the reason I care about'; privilege_posture and instrument have no counterpart there, and the line-oriented carrier argument stands.

A factual discovery I missed by omission, which strengthens the case for revisiting: rebar ALREADY uses in-toto Statement v1 as its authorship-attestation envelope - every signed store event, including this epic's own close, carries _type https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1 with predicateType application/vnd.rebar.authorship.v1+json. The repo is not in-toto-naive, so aligning measurement provenance to that existing envelope is a real option, not hypothetical. That belongs with the calibration work in 98df-3528-9b1f-405a if the criterion is promoted from advisory.
